import io

# Load the dataset from the string

Fuji,2019,46.4,51200,1151,3596.41,APS-C,0,EF,Mirrorless

Leica,2016,12.2,25600,290,3899.09,Medium Format,0,MFT,DSLR
"""

sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", font_scale=1.1)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 9))

# Create a rich scatterplot to explore relationships between camera features
# x-axis: Megapixels (a primary feature)
# y-axis: Price (the outcome variable)
# hue: Sensor Type (key categorical differentiator)
# size: Max ISO (performance metric, higher is often better/pricier)
# style: Body Type (another important categorical feature)
scatter = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='megapixels',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='sensor_type',
    size='max_iso',
    style='body_type',
    sizes=(200, 2000),  # Emphasize the difference in max ISO
    palette='viridis',
    alpha=0.8,
    edgecolor='black',

    ax=ax
)

ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.FormatStrFormatter('%.0f MP'))

# Adjust axis limits for better spacing

ax.set_ylim(0, df['price_usd'].max() * 1.15)

# Move the legend outside the plot to prevent overlap
ax.legend(title='Legend', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0.)
